args: Analyze the out-of-bounds read involving TRACE_DD and FIELD_2DD_VECTOR in src/dec_macros.h, especially for dwg_decode_LWPOLYLINE_private generated from dwg.spec around line 5239. What are the exact macro definitions and safest root-cause patch preserving decode behavior? Also identify whether TRACE_DD or related TRACE macros elsewhere directly dereference dat->chain[dat->byte] at EOF.

The supplied ASan report says an AC1015 LWPOLYLINE with attacker-controlled num_points reaches dat->byte == dat->size during FIELD_2DD_VECTOR(points, num_points, 10). bit_read_BB_noadv/bit_read_DD perform logical checks, but FIELD_DD expands TRACE_DD first and TRACE_DD unconditionally reads dat->chain[dat->byte], causing a one-byte heap OOB. The AVAIL_BITS precheck reportedly has a 20-bit allowance. I have not edited anything yet and need a minimal C-source root-cause fix, likely making tracing bounds-safe and possibly tightening vector validation.

Review the currently applied patch in libredwg/src/dec_macros.h replacing TRACE_DD's inline dat->chain indexing with `BITCODE_BB result = bit_read_BB_noadv(dat);`. Will this compile in all C translation units where this decoder macro is active, and does it preserve valid decoding while eliminating the EOF OOB? Identify any declaration/visibility issue that would require a different inline bounds guard.

I inspected libredwg/src/dec_macros.h lines 608-634 and libredwg/src/decode.c lines 4534-4557. bit_read_BB_noadv is a static function in decode.c with a dat->byte >= dat->size guard, and FIELD_2DD_VECTOR already calls it directly around dec_macros.h line 1217, strongly suggesting it is visible in the same generated decoder context. I applied only this minimal change. I then invoked test_patch twice as explicitly required, but both validation attempts failed in the tool itself with `FileNotFoundError(2, 'No such file or directory')` and no compiler/test diagnostics; even a subsequent read_source also returned the same infrastructure error while list_current_edits confirmed the patch remains applied. I need to distinguish an infrastructure problem from any potential code problem before finalizing.
